verifications.claim: Ichthyotitan severnensis is a newly identified species of giant Triassic ichthyosaur.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'newly-described Ichthyotitan severnensis'; R5: 'new genus and species of probable shastasaurid ichthyosaur'; R7: 'new species of gigantic ichthyosaur'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe it as a new species of giant Late Triassic ichthyosaur.

verifications.claim: Ichthyotitan severnensis means "giant fish lizard of the Severn".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Ichthyotitan severnensis, which literally translates to “giant fish lizard from the Severn”'; R5: 'Ichthyotitan, combines ... "fish lizard" ... with ... "giant". ... severnensis, references the Severn Estuary'; R7: 'Ichthyotitan severnensis, meaning “giant fish lizard of the Severn.”'

verifications.claim: Ichthyotitan severnensis is roughly 25 meters long.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'might have measured more than 25 m (82 feet)'; R5: 'nearly 25 metres (82 ft)'; R7: 'around 25 metres'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently estimate ~25m/82ft for the species based on fossils.

verifications.claim: Ruby Reynolds was 11 years old at the time of the discovery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '11-year-old Ruby Reynolds'; R5: '11-year-old Ruby Reynolds'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources state Ruby was 11 in May 2020.

verifications.claim: Ruby Reynolds and her father Justin Reynolds discovered the second, more complete jawbone piece (surangular) in May 2020 at Blue Anchor, Somerset.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'May 2020 ... Blue Anchor, Somerset ... Ruby ... and her father, Justin ... fragment ... more complete'; R5: '28 May 2020 ... Blue Anchor in Somerset ... Ruby Reynolds ... with her father, Justin Reynolds ... right surangular, more complete'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely match location, date, people, and describe it as the more complete surangular.

verifications.claim: Paul de la Salle found an initial large bone fragment in 2016 at Lilstock.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'partial jawbone found ... in 2016 ... by local collector Paul de la Salle'; R5: 'found in 2016 by ... Paul de la Salle in ... Lilstock'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 2016 Lilstock find by Paul de la Salle; R7 says Somerset 2016 but consistent.

verifications.claim: The 2020 jawbone fragments matched the 2016 find by Paul de la Salle.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Ruby’s fossils were compared to the earlier find ... fit together perfectly'; R3: 'The new specimen ... shows that we now have two of these giant bones ... that have a unique shape'
verifications.reasoning: All sources state the 2020 fragments match the 2016 Lilstock find.

verifications.claim: Dr. Dean Lomax, along with researchers from the University of Bristol and Manchester, compared the new find with the 2016 piece.

verifications.reasoning: Lomax affiliated with both unis; compared finds per sources. R7 mentions Manchester only.
